column1: # Every range over a map in rules/engine (non-test files), and maps.Keys/Values/All not sorted at once.
# Columns: function, ranged over, ordinal, body hash, functions of engineReach reached, calls not followed, class, why.
# SAFE: the result does not depend on the order. SORTED: the keys or results are sorted before they are used.
# A new range over a map fails TestEngineMapRanges until it is added here, read and classified;
# so does one whose body changed (its tokens, comments and line breaks aside), until it is read again
# and its new hash, from `go run ./internal/devtools/maprange rules/engine`, written here.

column8: Deletes every key equal to or under key; deletion during range is allowed and the resulting set does not depend on order.

Collects adds for keys only y has; x is not modified in this loop and keys are distinct, so the later application is order-independent. The calls not followed are the local closures look and both, which only read.
Each key of x is rewritten from its own entry and y's (y is read-only), or deleted; per-key independent, no budget. The calls not followed are the local closures look and both, which only read.

cleaned is sorted (slices.Sort) right after; edits order is irrelevant because applyCleans is commutative per key (taint=false, src OR) and edits keys are distinct. applyCleans sets taint=false and ORs src into each edit's own key, so applying edits in any order gives the same state; the edits are used by applyCleans only (refine, refineInPlace).
Returned keyRefs feed cleans' edits/cleaned; edits are applied commutatively (applyCleans) and cleaned is used only to fill sets (summ.checks set, a.guards map).
Builds a name set.
Init-time canonFuncs: out[lang] is appended per language in the fixed per-language list order; languages never interleave.
Budget is charged len(st) once before the loop; out is sorted by key (slices.SortFunc) before return.
Charge len(st) before the loop, then delete matching keys; order-independent.

Only adds to the e.watch set.
Builds byID; last-write-wins would matter only for duplicate rule IDs, which rules_test forbids (seen[r.ID] check). Values within each lang slice are in append order.

max over yielders: commutative while yields_to is acyclic (rules_test checks no cycle); a cycle would make levels depend on start order, but shipped rules cannot have one. The call not followed is the local closure level, which writes only yieldLevel.

Memoized longest-path levels on an acyclic graph are the same whatever key is started first (same caveat: cycles forbidden by rules_test). The call not followed is the local closure level, which writes only yieldLevel.
The collected conditions are only read to set c.leading = true when one has a URL context; an OR over them, so order does not matter.
all is only scanned to set c.leading = true (any); no order-sensitive use.
A name assigned two different classes anywhere ends in `two` and is deleted; every other name has a single class, so the final map is order-independent.
Deletes from vcls; order-independent.
desc[a] lists are in map order, but their only user, this(), filters them with pure memoized checks (callsParent) and slices.Sort(subs) before building the union key and infos.

s.sink[i] is deduped then sorted by (path,line) right after the loop (slices.SortFunc on s.sinkOf(i)); loc has only path and line, so the order is total. sinkEmb is an OR.
Builds sub map; the early `return nil` fires if any tainted non-literal member exists, which is order-independent.
